title: CoreWeave bonds plunge, yield hits 15% — warning sign for AI infrastructure financing
key_facts: CoreWeave bonds due 2032 fell below 80 cents on the dollar by 14 Oct; the yield rose to 14.8% (LSEG), against a 9.625% coupon at issue in June; the 2031 bonds traded near 14.9%.

CoreWeave total liabilities including leases were $52 billion at end-June (BigGo, citing the Financial Times); net interest payments in April-June were $640 million, up from $267 million a year earlier.
On 14 Oct CoreWeave shares fell 15%, Nebius 10%, Oracle 9%, Dell 10%, Arm 7%; the Nasdaq Composite closed down 1.9%; sector lost about $80 billion in value (BigGo, citing Bloomberg).
US September inflation was 3.7%, above expectations, raising bets on more rate rises.

Analysts quoted by BigGo expect the strain to push weaker, marginal borrowers out of financing markets rather than cause a wide default; Gartner projects 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations by 2030.

Startup Fortune: JPMorgan and MUFG have spent over six months trying to place a record $38 billion construction loan for Oracle-linked data centres in Texas and Wisconsin; less than $1 billion is left, and some lenders sell slices at a discount.
quote_evidence: Investors are increasingly questioning the debt-fueled growth model that has underpinned AI data center businesses. (BigGo)

Analysts believe the unraveling of the AI borrowing boom may not take the form of a systemic industry-wide default, but is more likely to manifest as weaker, marginal borrowers being gradually pushed out of financing markets. (BigGo)
why_it_matters_hint: Rising borrowing costs for AI data centre builders could shut weaker borrowers out of debt markets.
notes: FT page itself not readable; same story read at BigGo Finance and Startup Fortune. 'Darwin moment' is the FT headline wording only.
